reviews.text: The examinations are truly thorough, and everyone from the receptionists and staff to the head veterinarian is highly experienced. I've been a patient here for many years. They prioritize the well-being of the animals, so I feel at ease bringing my pets here.

It was quite some time ago, but my beloved dog was taken care of here. The doctors were very kind and always treated us warmly. He was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease and could not be saved, but I am grateful that they did their best to treat him. "I think he will pass away around this evening, so please spend the rest of your life at home," the doctor said, and he did indeed pass away that evening. Thanks to the doctor's words, we were able to be together as a family at the end. Thank you so much.
And, although you may have already passed away... thank you to Kuma-chan, who was kept at the clinic, for the blood transfusion⭐︎
We've been going to this clinic since our child was a baby. Everyone is so kind and welcoming, which puts me at ease.
Everyone is very polite, kind, and trustworthy.

It's a very good hospital, but it's too crowded.
The waiting room chairs are so cramped I can't sit comfortably.
The doctors are very kind.
It's so crowded I worry about what will happen in an emergency.
It's a very good veterinary hospital

The head veterinarian and all the other doctors at Nagaiki Animal Hospital are so kind and always willing to give me advice about my dog ​​(*^^)v
I've been going to them for decades now (*^^)v

He's a really good doctor. He performed the procedure right in front of me and only performed the bare minimum of examinations.
He diagnosed me through physical examination and his explanations were easy to understand, so I felt completely at ease and could leave my condition in his care.

My senior dog was in critical condition on Thursday (a day when my regular vet was closed). Desperate, I called this vet, which is open on Thursdays, explaining the situation and asking if they could see him as an emergency case. However, they said they were fully booked and couldn't accommodate me.

While I understand that hospitals have their own schedules, I was appalled that they wouldn't even consider accepting a dying elderly dog, especially as a veterinary clinic, let alone a specialist hospital.

Incidentally, I called another vet in a neighboring town, and they kindly accepted my dog, saving his life. I am very grateful to that vet.

I often encounter pet owners in my neighborhood who recommend this vet, but upon closer inspection, some say their earliest appointment was four days away. I wonder if that's acceptable for someone working in veterinary medicine.

We have been taking care of both dogs and cats for many years. 
The rescue cat we adopted was prone to catching colds and almost died once, but thanks to the efforts of the director and all the staff, he miraculously recovered and is now healthy again. We are very grateful.
